sentences.text: Pseudorhina belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes sharks and rays.
Two species, P. acanthoderma and P. alifera, are distinguished by differences in body size, proportions, and tooth anatomy.
It is currently considered the oldest known genus of angel shark.
Full body fossils of these species are known from the Late Jurassic Solnhofen Plattenkalk limestones of southern Germany.
The genus Pseudorhina was described by Jaekel in 1898.
Its classification was later revised by Klug and Kriwet in 2012.
The genus Pseudorhina is placed in the monotypic family Pseudorhinidae.
Fossils of Pseudorhina are known from the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous periods of Europe.
The time range for Pseudorhina is from the Toarcian to the Valanginian, between 182.9 and 132.6 million years ago.
